data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Laina is the name of a nymph who personified the gentle flow of rivers. The name is derived from the Greek word 'leinan', meaning 'to flow'. In Christianity, Laina is also associated with the Virgin Mary, whose maternal love flows endlessly. The name Laina carries the meaning “Delicate flow” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Laina usually hope their child will grow to embody delicate flow and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Laina

data.cultural_impact: In Greek mythology, Laina is a name associated with the ever-flowing and gentle force of nature. It is the name of a nymph who personified the peaceful flow of rivers. (Some sources also associate Laina with the Greek goddess Lalaina, who presided over the passage of the sun and the changing of the seasons). This name has been carried through history, and today it is sometimes given to girls to reflect the flowing, graceful nature associated with it.
data.spiritual_significance: In the context of the Christian faith, Laina takes on new meaning. The name is also associated with the Virgin Mary, whose maternal love flows endlessly. Mary is known as the "fountain of living water," (John 4:14) and her love for her Son provides a constant source of spiritual nourishment for believers. The gentle flow of the river Laina can be seen as a reflection of Mary's loving, nurturing relationship with her Son and with all of humanity. Laina is a reminder of the eternal, loving flow of the divine presence in the world.
